text: ARM, Bicep, and CloudFormation are all real, officially supported tools that solve the exact problem this chapter raised: describing an end state instead of a sequence of steps, with idempotency and drift detection built in. But they share one catch worth naming directly before this course moves on from Infrastructure as Code previews.

Bicep compiles to ARM, and ARM only exists inside Azure. CloudFormation is native to AWS and doesn't exist anywhere outside it. Neither limitation is a design flaw — Microsoft and Amazon both built their tool tightly around their own platform, on purpose — but pick either one, and you've also quietly picked a cloud.

Terraform, from HashiCorp, is declarative in exactly the same way — end state, computed changes, drift detection for free. What's different is scope: Terraform talks to whichever provider plugin you load, with providers for Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and hundreds of other platforms, all through the same CLI and the same HCL configuration language.

An Azure-only team can reasonably pick Bicep. An AWS-only team can reasonably pick CloudFormation. Both are genuinely good, real choices. But a team running both faces a harder question with either native tool — two syntaxes, two tool sets, two sets of tribal knowledge, forever — and that's exactly the question Terraform's provider model removes.

That's not a theoretical preference. Terraform has become the real industry standard specifically for multi-cloud and hybrid teams, precisely because of that provider model, and a person's Terraform skills transfer directly between employers even when they run on entirely different clouds — one real, practical reason this path gives Terraform an entire next course.

This lesson previewed why, on purpose, without teaching Terraform syntax, state files, or providers in depth — that's the Terraform & Bicep course's job next, in the Advanced Specialization stage. Before that, Chapter 6 returns to scripted automation, starting with automating VM start and stop schedules for real cost savings.
